review.tagline: Distributed Python runtime with libraries for data, training, tuning, RL and serving
review.summary: Ray is a distributed runtime for scaling Python code from a laptop to a cluster, built around tasks, actors and shared objects. On top of the core it ships libraries for datasets (Data), distributed training (Train), hyperparameter tuning (Tune), reinforcement learning (RLlib) and model serving (Serve). It includes a dashboard and a distributed debugger, and runs on local machines, clusters, cloud providers and Kubernetes.
review.audience: Python and ML engineers scaling workloads across machines or clusters
strengths: Same Python code scales from one machine to a cluster without extra infrastructure
One runtime covers data processing, training, tuning, RL and serving
Runs on bare clusters, cloud providers and Kubernetes
Ships a dashboard and a distributed debugger for cluster apps
weaknesses: Python-centric; README describes scaling Python applications only
Broad scope with many libraries means a large surface to learn
README gives no hardware requirements or cluster sizing guidance
Anyscale managed offering is promoted; OSS versus hosted feature split is unclear
